title: Agents scaled up from homeostatic loops by adding memory, anticipation and networks

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Agents scaled up from homeostatic loops by adding memory, anticipation and networks

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Agents evolved by scaling up from basic homeostatic loops (whose set points are the first goals), driven by surprise minimization, through the successive addition of delays (memory), anticipation (inference), and spatially distributed networks that allow learning and abstraction.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Conclusion and Future Outlook

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Agents scaled up by evolving from basic homeostatic loops, driven by active inference (surprise minimization) via addition of delays (memory), anticipation (inference), and networks (spatially-distributed processing that enables learning and progressive abstraction/generalization from data).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition”, Frontiers in psychology (2019), doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02688; section “Conclusion and Future Outlook”. Scope: Evolution of agency from early living systems to complex organisms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2019-boundary-22: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.28

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public phylogenetic and molecular data can test a coarse ordering of component innovations. They cannot establish the proposed active-inference driver or a single universal scaling path for agency.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Map the phylogenetic appearance of homeostatic feedback, persistent state, predictive control, and distributed networks, and test whether their inferred ordering matches the proposed sequence and correlates with expanded behavioral capacities.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Abstract capacities do not map one-to-one onto genes.

Ancient evolutionary ordering is weakly recoverable from extant systems.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.3
discriminating power: 0.2
analysis feasibility: 0.28
data existence: 0.45
data adequacy: 0.15

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The closing summary states how agents scaled up, by adding memory, anticipation, and networks to homeostatic loops under surprise minimization. Extant physiology can be described in those terms in more than one order. No dataset records the succession. The claim is a historical schema without a distinguishing test.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Homeostasis, memory, and prediction can be ascribed to living systems after the fact. A required evolutionary sequence from loops, through delays, to networks is not a variable in phylogenetic or experimental datasets.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Alternative orders of the same ingredients fit the same modern organisms.

The scaling path is a narrative of how agency must have been built.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.22
discriminating power: 0.08
analysis feasibility: 0.1
data existence: 0.05
data adequacy: 0.05
